name: Salesmessage
summary: Business texting and SMS marketing in one shared inbox. Reach customers where they actually reply with two-way texting, automation and team collaboration.
best_for: sales and service teams that want two-way texting and calling in one CRM-linked inbox, and can estimate their monthly credit burn, messages plus call minutes, before they sign
skip_if: your audience doesn't respond to SMS, or your volume is low enough that the fixed 10DLC overhead outweighs the sending. Also skip it if you need a lot of seats cheaply. And skip it if your real usage lands in the gap between the $25 and $329 plans, since the only bridge on offer is a bigger credit bundle on the small plan
honest_knock: Two things changed here and both cost money. First, calling now runs on the same meter as texting (1 credit a minute, 2 a minute when forwarding) so voice minutes eat the allowance you budgeted for messages. Second, the plan cards jump from $25 to $329 a month, but the credits dropdown fills the gap ($49, $99, $179 and $249 a month on Basic) and raises your allowance without adding a single seat. Size the credits, not the headcount. An MMS is 2 credits, so one picture message to 1,000 contacts is 2,000 credits: four times the entire monthly allowance on Basic. Seats and numbers bill on top of every plan beyond the first of each: a five-person team on one number is $40 a month over the sticker, and the annual headline of $21 and $277 is a per-month display of a bill charged yearly. Note what the page has stopped saying since our previous check: there is no published per-credit overage rate anymore, so what happens when you run out mid-cycle is not stated where you buy: ask before you commit. And US business texting carries a regulatory layer of its own: 10DLC registration and carrier surcharges bill separately from anything quoted here, and opt-in and opt-out handling stays your legal responsibility: the platform enables compliance, it does not absolve you.

pricing.entry_price_terms: Basic (500 message credits a month) · on monthly billing, as published
pricing.notes: (2026-08-08, re-verified 10 September, 13 October and 13 November 2026 on www.salesmessage.com/pricing in both billing modes) Repackaged since our last check into two named plans plus Enterprise, metered in message credits. Monthly billing: Basic is $25 a month for 500 credits a month; Pro is $329 a month for 10,000 credits a month; Enterprise is contact-for-pricing with custom credits. Both plans carry a credits dropdown that raises the allowance for a fixed add-on. On Basic, 1,000 credits is +$24, 2,500 is +$74, 5,000 is +$154 and 7,500 is +$224 a month. On Pro the ladder runs from 15,000 credits at +$150 up to 50,000 at +$1,170 a month, in 5,000-credit steps. Annual billing is shown as two months free. Basic is $21 a month billed yearly for 6,000 credits a year (12,000 credits +$252, 30,000 +$756, 60,000 +$1,560, 90,000 +$2,268), and Pro $277 a month billed yearly for 120,000 credits a year (180,000 +$1,512, rising to 600,000 at +$11,796). Seats and numbers are priced apart from the plan: the first seat is free and each additional seat is $10.00 a month or $100.00 a year; the first number is free and each additional number is $5.00 a month or $50.00 a year. The page defines the meter itself: SMS is 1 credit per 160 characters, MMS is 2 credits, calling is 1 credit a minute and call forwarding is 2 credits a minute. A 14-day free trial runs, and a 30-day money-back guarantee is offered, refunded less the message credits used. When we tried to sign up on 18 November 2026, the registration page required a credit card and a US mobile number before the account opened: the button read 'Start my free trial' under 'Try 14 days free, then just $61 per month'. We entered nothing and stopped there. The page no longer publishes a per-credit overage rate, nor terms for taxes, carrier fees or country availability, so we quote none.

exit_test.what: Daan started the sign-up himself; the registration page asked for a credit card and a US mobile number before any account opened, so no account was created. On 18 November 2026 the session reached the registration page of Salesmessage and stopped there: before an account opened, the page required a credit card and a US mobile number. The button read Start my free trial, with the line Try 14 days free, then just $61 per month above it. Nothing was filled in, no account opened and the product itself was not tested. Account and start: Daan opened the registration page of Salesmessage (app.salesmessage.com/register) on the evening of 18 November 2026 and passed on what it showed; the interface was in English. The dossier name is Salesmessage and the review is on ZTS (zts/salesmessage-review.html). What the registration page required: before an account opened, the page required a credit card and a US mobile number. The button read Start my free trial, with the line Try 14 days free, then just $61 per month above it. Stop: nothing was filled in and nothing was started, so no account was opened and no trial began. The core function, the text message inbox and the credit use per message, was therefore not tested. Screenshots: none were made, because the screen showed Daan's own details; there is no image to check or mask. Cancelling: not applicable, because no trial or plan was started. Not tested: everything after the registration page, which means the inbox, sending a message, the credit use per message, the trial itself, checkout, tax and the final price. Clean up: there is no account, no trial and no test data; nothing was sent or bought. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: The registration page required a credit card and a US mobile number before an account opened, although the button says Start my free trial. A buyer outside the US without a US mobile number may not get past this page, and a card is needed before the free trial starts.
